title: SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE — Security Classification Guide for the LANTERN Training Sensor (NOT REAL GUIDANCE)
introduction: This synthetic guide shows each kind of OpenSCG entry: an unclassified element, classified elements, a level range with conditions, an exemption, and a compilation.

entries.description: The program name LANTERN and the fact that the program exists.
The identity of the sponsoring office.
The maximum detection range of the sensor, stated as a specific figure.
entries.reason: 1.4(a), 1.4(e). Synthetic rationale: knowing the exact range would let an adversary plan to stay just outside it.
entries.declassification: 25 years from the date the record was created

entries.description: The operating frequency band of the sensor.
entries.level: U to C: Unclassified when stated only as a general band name. Confidential when stated to within 10 MHz.
entries.level_conditions: Unclassified when stated only as a general band name. Confidential when stated to within 10 MHz.
entries.reason: 1.4(e). Synthetic rationale: a precise band would make the sensor easier to jam.

entries.description: Specific conditions under which the sensor fails to detect a target.
entries.reason: 1.4(g). Synthetic rationale: describes a vulnerability of the system.
entries.declassification: On event: Retirement of the last fielded LANTERN unit, as announced by the program office.

entries.description: The sponsoring office together with the operating band, in the same document.
entries.reason: 1.4(a). Synthetic rationale: together they reveal a mission focus that neither reveals alone.
entries.declassification: 10 years from the date the record was created
entries.condition: Both items appear together in a way that associates the band with this sponsor.
